text.p: Israeli bonds closed mixed on Monday amid expectations of a cut in interest rates later this month, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.12 pct to 105.3
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 to 104.09

"There was big demand for unlinked bonds because consumer price indices (CPI) are expected to be low after April and there are expectations in the market that there will be a cut in interest rates," said Adam Reuter, managing director of Financial Immunities consultancy.
"The market believes the cut will be made given the extent of the recession and following today's budget meeting," he said.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel met on Sunday evening to discuss the budget deficit but no decision was reached and the talks will resume on Monday afternoon.
It is unclear whether any decision to cut the budget will be made at the meeting and the central bank has refused to link a budget cut to a reduction in interest rates.

"Buyers are turning to unlinked bonds, while trade in CPI-linked bonds was mixed, on expectations of lower inflation. There was total demand of about 420 million shekels for unlinked bonds and Makams," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.

"The market expects an interest rate cut of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point," Halpern said. Prices of long and medium-term CPI-linked bonds were down while prices of short-term CPI-linked bonds were slightly higher, he said.
"There was also demand for dollar-linked bonds because the dollar continues to strengthen in the world and on expectations of lower interest rates," he added.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
